item.stem:
The diagram shows house $H$ and shop $S$ on the same side of straight path $L$. Kavya must walk from $H$ to a point $P$ on $L$, then to $S$, and wants the shortest broken path $H$-$P$-$S$. Point $S'$ is the reflection of $S$ across $L$.

Which claim correctly chooses $P$?

options.A: Take $P$ as the foot of the perpendicular from $H$ to $L$ alone, and ignore $S$ and $S'$.
options.B: Call the answer line only, with no choice of $P$ on $L$.
options.C: Join $H$ to $S'$ by a straight segment; let $P$ be where that segment meets $L$.
options.D: Reflection still chooses $P$ even when $S'$ is not the same distance from $L$ as $S$ is.
